overview: This Senate resolution states that Hamas, the armed group that has governed the Gaza Strip since 2007 and that the State Department has listed as a foreign terrorist organization since 1997, cannot be allowed to keep any political or military control of Gaza. Its opening section recounts the group's founding charter, the October 7, 2023 attack on Israel that killed more than 1,200 people and took more than 250 hostages, and U.S. government findings that Iran funds and arms Hamas. The resolution calls on the President to use every economic and diplomatic tool available to cut off Hamas's money from Iran and other sources, and it expresses support for Israel as it defends itself against Hamas, Iran, and groups backed by Iran. It is a statement of the Senate's position and does not change any law. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on March 13, 2025.
for: Supporters say it puts the Senate clearly on record that any lasting arrangement for Gaza must not leave a designated terrorist group in charge, and it presses the administration to choke off the funding that lets Hamas rearm.
against: Critics say the resolution does not address who should govern Gaza instead or the needs of civilians there, and as a nonbinding statement it sets a goal without any plan or resources to achieve it.
